text: A little world of your own. The name comes from Arthur C. Clarke's novel Rendezvous with Rama (1973). In the book, Rama is a sealed, cylindrical, self-contained world that carries everything it needs inside it. That matches the product's core design: Like Clarke's Rama, which inspired the name, RamaSite is a complete world of its own. What it does: If something is missing, the site says what on its first visit, in words you can pass on to your host. The admin is at /admin . See Getting started for what to do next. If you have Composer and PHP on the machine that will run the site, you can install from Packagist in place of steps 1 and 2: composer create-project dalefranks/ramasite mysite --no-dev That fetches the same files as the release zip, with the vendor folder. As with the zip, the site writes its settings file and creates its database on its first visit. Put the mysite folder where your web server serves it, then carry on from step 3. To upgrade later, upload a newer release zip's files over it, as below. Your pages, images, settings and accounts aren't in the release zip, so uploading a new version never overwrites them. How each part of the admin works: docs . RamaSite is free and open-source software under the MIT License . Copyright (c) 2026 Dale Franks. RamaSite is built with Laravel and Filament, using SQLite. composer install cp .env.example .env php artisan key:generate php artisan migrate php artisan test Releases are built by GitHub Actions when a tag starting with v is pushed: the tests and a package security check run, then the zip (with the vendor folder) is published. A tag with a hyphen, such as v0.4.0-alpha , is published as a pre-release.
